lead: Dr. Pham Thi Thu Hien (Dr. Hailey) is a general and restorative dentist. She believes the best treatment isn't always the biggest one: by keeping as much healthy tooth as possible, she helps patients get conservative, natural-looking restorations that are built to last.

p: Dr. Hailey provides general and restorative dentistry, from routine care to veneers, ceramic crowns, inlays and onlays, with a focus on conservative, long-lasting results.
She chose dentistry to help patients keep their own teeth healthy for as long as possible, and plans every restoration around the tooth structure that can be saved.

journeyMeta.intro: Most veneer and crown cases are completed in one trip, depending on how many teeth are treated.

faqs.q: How do I know whether I need veneers or crowns?
faqs.a: Veneers may suit teeth that need a change in shape or colour and still have enough healthy enamel. Crowns are usually considered when a tooth is significantly weakened or heavily restored. The choice is made after an examination.

faqs.q: Can a tooth become infected again after root canal treatment?
faqs.a: It can. Reinfection may come from missed canals, leakage, new decay, cracks or a poor final restoration. Careful cleaning and sealing, ideally under a microscope, and a well-fitting final restoration help prevent it.

faqs.q: What are the options for replacing missing teeth?
faqs.a: Depending on how many teeth are missing and the condition of the neighbouring teeth and bone, options include dental implants, implant-supported bridges, conventional bridges or removable dentures.

faqs.q: How long does orthodontic treatment usually take?
faqs.a: Many cases take 12–24 months, but it depends on how complex the bite is, the method (braces or clear aligners) and how consistently the plan is followed. You get an estimate in writing after your examination.
You receive a written quote after your examination, before any treatment starts. Anything that depends on what we find during treatment is explained and quoted as a range up front.
